title: E-RLT-0115: a bound register pair on the candidate rule moves the same in all 13 husk directions, fail as registered...
purpose: Experiment E-RLT-0115 in the relativity arena: a bound register pair on the candidate rule moves the same in all 13 husk directions, fail as registered on its off-line residual: on the swap coin built into the Cl+(4) register (E-FND-0177's surviving variant, which every bound-pair engine already runs) E-SPN-0173's pair at $a_B$ 3.5 has one $K^2$ coefficient 0.0183178 over the 3 axes, 6 face and 4 body diagonals and a generic direction, spread 2.3e-6, against 0.158 for the working rule's lineon over the same 13 (0.199 on a grid), and the lighter-bound $a_B$ 6 pair (R 2.72, E-SPN-0200's axis read reproduced to the bit) agrees on an axis, a body and a face diagonal to 1.5e-3; its first direction-dependent term is $K^4$ (-0.0037 on the axes to -0.0025 on the body diagonals); after the reduced engine's fix (the (1, 1, -1) and (1, -1, 1) sectors built as images of (1, 1, 1)'s, every other sector bit for bit unchanged) all four body diagonals read the same base and shift 4.01e-4 at kappa 0.16, but their residual 9.84e-4 is above the 2.3e-4 the registered gate calls stuck, and it is the level's own floor (1.5e-3 at K 0, 1.0e-3 on the axis), not line branching, so mobility off lines is read in E-RLT-0116 and E-RLT-0117.
known_limitations: Depth L2 (L2: known physics reproduced on a stated model).
